- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 15–30% for early periods.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 5x historical mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 3x recent 7-day high.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 10–20% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- Model overreacts to sentiment spikes; if sentiment jumps >0.67 in 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 20–40% to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates in low-sentiment periods; apply a 10–15% upward bias when sentiment <0.33.
- If history shows mean reversion (price oscillates within 0.5–1.0 range), model overpredicts direction; use 20–30% smoothing on forecast to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture sentiment shift; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day mean to adjust forecast.
